text:
Priya: quick heads-up — observed steady memory growth on prod-canary when long contexts hit continuous-batcher merge path. looks like KV slab regeneration keeps allocating.
Ben: reproable on staging? any flamegraph or heap profile yet?
Priya: yes repro on staging. captured a heap profile at ~30m into the run. attaching snippets below.
Priya: ```
# go tool pprof -http=:6060 kv_cache_heap.pb
TotalAlloc: 1.2GB
Inuse: 940MB
Top allocators:
  kv::slot_entry      420MB  (40%)
  kv::fragment_buf    260MB  (28%)
  runtime.mspan       120MB  (12%)
``` 
Samir: oof slot_entry that high suggests reuse isn't happening. are merges creating transient fragments that never get consolidated?
Priya: hypothesis: when cont-batcher merges incoming small requests into one head batch, we split into fragments for each trace, then merge-window expiry causes duplicate slot allocations instead of reusing existing slots.
Taylor: could be an ordering race — head-of-line blocking holds onto the new merged descriptor, preventing the reclamation path from reattaching freed slots until the merge completes.
Nina: any quick logs showing evict/pin sequences? those help show whether the reclaim loop is signaled.
Priya: snippet from staging logs — look for kv_reclaim signals around merge:
Priya: ```
[2026-03-10T14:05:12Z] kv: merge window open id=0x7c2
[2026-03-10T14:05:12Z] kv: alloc slot s=0x9f2 size=24KB owner=batch-merge
[2026-03-10T14:05:12Z] scheduler: contbatch: head wait for slots
[2026-03-10T14:05:12Z] kv: reclaim-signal sent
[2026-03-10T14:05:12Z] kv: reclaim deferred due to headlock
[2026-03-10T14:05:23Z] kv: alloc slot s=0xa12 size=24KB owner=batch-merge
[2026-03-10T14:05:32Z] kv: evict candidate s=0x9f2 but pinned
``` 
Ben: "reclaim deferred due to headlock" — that's the crux. can we change reclaim to opportunistically reuse pinned slots once merge finishes, not wait for explicit GC?
Samir: short-term mitigation: reduce merge window and increase slot reuse threshold. if we shrink merge_window from 100ms->20ms, fewer simultaneous fragment allocations.
Taylor: but that may harm latency for small requests if we merge less aggressively. tradeoff.
Priya: perf-bot ran a quick A/B on staging with MERGE_WINDOW=25ms + KV_REUSE_THRESHOLD=1. Results: ~18% drop in steady-state mem and 5% p50 latency increase for <64 token traces.
perf-bot: @Priya A/B results uploaded: https://internal.perf/reports/2410001111-merge-tuning
Nina: long-term: consider adding a merge-completion hook that triggers reclaim/slot-coalescing before spawning next allocation. basically move from passive GC to deterministic coalescing on merge end.
Ben: agree. also add per-batch trace id for fragments so coalescer can group and compact contiguous fragments into single slab entries.
Samir: I'll prototype a coalescer that runs inline at merge end, but offloaded to low-priority worker to avoid blocking critical path. it will attempt to fold any fragments with contiguous offsets.
Priya: thanks. action items: Samir proto + perf run (staging), Taylor to model latency impact for small requests, Nina to add observability (slot pin/unpin counters + reclaim latency histogram). I'll follow up with flamegraphs after the next run.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Priya: one more note — we found one edge where quantized models cause slightly larger fragment_bufs which increases chance of fragmentation; include that in the test matrix.
Taylor: noted. I'll add quantized-large and quantized-small cases.
Priya: cool. cc @eng-runtime for visibility. will post update when staging completes.
